description: Firm Portal-BC purchase-order twins (ontology.identity_scoring.corroborate_po_twins, the twins build step) over the session's live projection: scripts.po_twin_probe opens ontology.session_projection's {session_state}/ontology.sqlite read-only and, offline with no client, counts the BC purchase orders, the number-text leads of PurchaseOrder.same_record_as, the corroborated same_record rows the build wrote, and judges every lead again without writing (outcome per code: firm, ambiguous, rejected, already_firm, lineage_not_authority, number_not_exact, supplier_conflict, supplier_not_agreed, supplier_ambiguous, conflict, no_secondary_agreement), with up to three samples as outcome, feature names and evidence counts per scheme. It also records leads per number-series pair (lead_shapes, masked) and the supplier verdicts the outcomes imply. Pass = exit 0, at least one BC order with a firm twin (a firm count of 0 is never a pass), nothing written through the connection, and the written firm twins equal the leads judged firm now. Counts, codes and scheme names only; never a value, key, identifier, citation or name. Live-unverified until the verifier records a result.
notes: Registered, live-unverified: no verifier result yet. Module test: isolated-fixture (ontology/tests/test_po_identity_firm.py runs this spec's argv over a synthetic projection and checks it with live_verify.check_expectations). A firm count of 0 fails. On the flagship captured state it is 0: every lead pairs a BC PO###### number with the Portal order whose number was rewritten to it, and the supplier names conflict on 180 of 186 (the date or total on 6); the vendor-number masks differ, so no code is compared. Reader is the service; the read tools apply each reader's scope on top (corroborated links fall to lead when a reader cannot read what they cite).
